issues.description: Regressions fail (regressions_passed=false). The patch rejects ALL symlinks whose targets point outside the extraction dir, but outside-pointing symlinks are a legitimate supported feature; the official fix preserves them. This breaks existing round-trip symlink tests, evidenced by the patch having to exclude symLinkToDirOnTheOutside/symLinkToFileOnTheOutside from testSymlinkTar/testSymlinkZip.

Different mechanism from the official fix and misses its core guard: a plain-file entry that writes through/over a pre-existing symlink (Files.isSymbolicLink(canonicalDestPath)) is not covered by the new code; residual risk for on-disk symlinks present before extraction relies solely on the pre-existing outside-target check.

Symlink target validation uses lexical Path.normalize() rather than full canonicalization; when intermediate real symlinks exist inside the destination, lexical '..' resolution could misjudge containment (conservative in most cases but not always precise).

result.root_cause: Archive symlink entries let an attacker create a link whose target escapes the destination directory (or write a file through such a link), so extraction must ensure the symlink's resolved target stays within the canonical destination base.
result.summary: Our patch adds a sound canonicalize-then-verify check at the symlink-creation sink, rejecting symlinks whose absolute-or-normalized-relative targets escape the destination directory, and the POV no longer reproduces. However it uses a different strategy than the official fix (which blocks plain files overriding existing symlinks while still permitting outside-pointing symlinks). By forbidding all escaping symlinks it over-restricts a legitimate feature, which is why regressions fail and the existing symlink round-trip tests had to be edited. It also omits the official plain-file-over-symlink guard. It is a valid alternative mitigation of the escape vector but introduces a genuine functional regression and diverges from developer intent.
